# Do not edit by hand: run the tool (docs/45). This file is what the About page lists.
# name<TAB>version<TAB>dir<TAB>license<TAB>what
alarms	0.1.0	lib/alarms		The alarm queue: one ordered list, only the nearest deadline is armed.
board_atom	0.1.0	lib/board_atom		Who this firmware is for: the M5 ATOM Lite. Headers only: board/identity.h says the name and how many lights the strip has, board/impl.h says what to link.
board_esp32	0.1.0	lib/board_esp32		Who this firmware is for: a plain ESP32 and nothing else, the smallest band the system has to fit in. Headers only: board/identity.h says the name and what it has not got, board/impl.h says what to link.
board_matrix	0.1.0	lib/board_matrix		Who this firmware is for: the M5 ATOM Matrix, the same band as the Lite with a panel of twenty-five lights. Headers only.
board_paper	0.1.0	lib/board_paper		Who this firmware is for: the M5 Paper v1.0 and v1.1 (K049 and K049-B), 16 MB of flash, 8 MB of PSRAM and the pin map of the e-ink band. Headers only: board/identity.h says the name, board/impl.h says what to link.
board_tkoala	0.1.0	lib/board_tkoala		Who this firmware is for: the LilyGO TTGO T-Koala (ESP32-WROVER-B). Headers only: board/identity.h says the name, one plain LED and no IMU; board/impl.h says what to link.
epub	0.1.0	lib/epub	MIT	The XHTML of a chapter of a book, word by word with the byte of each word: the blocks, the entities as Latin-1, the pictures with their side, and the grid of a table. No allocation of its own.
hal	0.1.0	lib/hal		Hardware abstraction interfaces: capabilities, clock, storage, net, power.
hal_atom	0.2.0	lib/hal_atom		Board support for the M5 ATOM family (Lite and Matrix): ESP32-PICO-D4, one button on GPIO39, one light or twenty-five on GPIO27, and the MPU6886 of the Matrix. The drivers for the things it puts on a pin, and everything else that is the chip's, are in hal_esp32.
hal_emulator	0.1.0	lib/hal_emulator		Board support for the PC emulator: same kernel, host console, host disk.
hal_esp32	0.1.0	lib/hal_esp32		The parts of the hardware that belong to the ESP32 itself and not to a board: LittleFS, the NVS store, the SoC clock, the sleep, the radio (esp_wifi, provisioning, NTP and a page) and the capabilities it gives every board. Also the drivers for what a board puts on a pin or a bus —keys read from GPIO, a strip of WS2812 and a card in an SD slot— because the reading is the chip's and the hardware is the board's (docs/50).
hal_paper	0.2.0	lib/hal_paper		Board support for the M5 Paper (v1.0 and v1.1): ESP32-D0WDQ6-V3, 16 MB of flash, 8 MB of PSRAM, the main power hold on GPIO2 and a dial of three keys. What is the chip's, including the reader of those keys and the radio, is in hal_esp32. The e-ink panel, the touch, the RTC chip, the gauge are not here yet (docs/50, docs/90).
hal_tkoala	0.1.0	lib/hal_tkoala		Board support for the LilyGO TTGO T-Koala: ESP32-WROVER-B, 4 MB of flash, 8 MB of PSRAM (4 mapped), a green LED on GPIO5, the BOOT key on GPIO0 and a microSD slot on the HSPI pins. The drivers for the chip and the card are in hal_esp32.
img	0.1.0	lib/img		The pictures a page can carry, read the way this project reads everything: the file is the caller's bytes, the rows come out four bits a pixel, and there is no allocation of its own (docs/30).
inflate	0.1.0	lib/inflate		Deflate read the other way (RFC 1951) and the two checksums a container needs (RFC 1950, zip), with no allocation of its own.
json	0.1.0	lib/json		Pull-style JSON helpers: read one known key, never build a tree.
kernel	0.1.0	lib/kernel		lunokOS kernel: boot, event loop, shell, log ring.
lua	5.4.7	lib/lua	MIT	Lua 5.4.7 sources, vendored so luaconf.h can be tuned for the board.
luabind	0.1.0	lib/luabind		The Lua state, its accounting allocator and the first bindings.
pal	0.1.0	lib/pal		Platform abstraction layer: queues, console, log sink, clock, reboot.
pal_esp32	0.1.0	lib/pal_esp32		PAL implementation for ESP32 + Arduino (FreeRTOS queue, UART console).
pal_host	0.1.0	lib/pal_host		PAL implementation for POSIX (emulator): in-memory queue and raw stdin/stdout console.
qr	0.1.0	lib/qr		A QR code that can be any QR: every version of the standard, every level of error correction and the three modes that carry text. Written here so it can be read, with the tables the standard publishes.
ttf	0.1.0	lib/ttf	MIT	TrueType outlines read the way a page needs them: the tables of a font, the glyph of a code, and the outline of that glyph drawn at the size it is asked for. Since 0.150.0 it also opens the box a face travels in, a WOFF of a book (docs/46, D6).
zip	0.1.0	lib/zip	MIT	The ZIP container an EPUB travels in: the closing record, the central directory and one entry inflated into a block of the caller's, with no allocation of its own.
